topic.title: We buy air purifiers for the number on the screen
topic.claim: An air purifier sells because it turns invisible air into a number you can watch, and we pay for what we can see.
topic.behaviour: People compare purifiers by room size, filter type and the live AQI display. Sales are up across India, not only in Delhi.
topic.mechanism: Clean air has no visible result. A glowing number gives the buyer proof that money is working, and gives the brand a screen to sell.
topic.group: Urban families worried about air but unsure what to buy
topic.moment: You sit in a room watching the AQI number on a small screen fall from 300 to 80 and feel the purchase was worth it.

turn.believed: You buy a purifier because the air is bad.
turn.actually: You buy it for the display that shows it's fixed. We pay for the number we can watch.

topic.feeling: relieved that something visible finally shows the problem is being handled
topic.villain: a market where invisible benefits only sell when they come with a screen
topic.because: A live reading builds trust and justifies a premium. It also creates a reason to keep watching and keep the purifier running.

proof.fact: Amazon India said air-purifier sales doubled in the last week, and Amazon says shoppers now compare models by room size, filter type and live AQI sensors.

topic.payoff: Test it: would you have bought the same purifier with the screen covered?
topic.send_to: The friend who bought a purifier and checks the number first thing in the morning.
real_details: Versuni India's Pooja Baid says buyers are purchasing earlier, a shift from panic-driven to proactive adoption.
topic.news_peg: Amazon India reports air-purifier sales doubled in the last week, reported 2026-11-17
topic.why_now: Delhi-NCR air has turned toxic and purifier demand is spreading beyond the city.

score.why: We pay for the number we can watch: the visible-versus-invisible belief, in a purchase people are making this month.
